mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% indicates tighter monetary conditions, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, positively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 35% of cases when UNRATE is below 6%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) show concurrent increases, it indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of cases when both UNRATE and PAYEMS are rising, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5% increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which may lead to increased corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when GDPC1 increases by more than 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates easier monetary conditions, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, positively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 45% of cases when FEDFUNDS is low, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 35% of cases when INDPRO increases by more than 1%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises faster than the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), it indicates inflationary pressures that may erode corporate margins and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when CPIAUCSL rises faster than FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 45% of cases when HOUST increases by more than 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.
